stemMd: At 25 °C, an aqueous solution has pH 9. What is its hydroxide-ion concentration, using pH + pOH = 14?
explanationMd: First pOH = 14 − 9 = 5. Since pOH = −log₁₀[OH⁻], the hydroxide concentration is 10⁻⁵ mol/L. The value exceeds 10⁻⁷, consistent with a basic solution.

distractorRationale.b: This confuses the water ion product with one ion concentration.
distractorRationale.d: This reverses the sign in the negative-log relation.
distractorRationale.e: This is the neutral concentration at the stated temperature.
